messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#INC-9943 -> network-prod-lb-health (threshold: 5% TLS errors) https://pagerduty.com/INC-9943
Priya K: acked in PD, I'm on it — triaging ALB logs + edge metrics now.
Marco L: seeing spike in TLS handshake failures from edge->backend starting ~4332109600, matches PD window. 502/504 rate up ~9% on eu-west-1.
Jules (oncall): @Priya K @Marco L I'm taking primary. if this looks like cert or SNI issue I'll start failover checklist.
Priya K: quick grep from edge logs: `tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate` for host `api.redwood-inference.com`
Priya K: sample curl failing: ```curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/health -H 'Host: api.redwood-inference.com'``` -> `* SSL: certificate subject name 'internal.lb.local' does not match 'api.redwood-inference.com'`
Marco L: that points to wrong cert on some targets. checking recent deploys — there was a certificate rotation job 15m ago (deploybot: cert-rotation/2023-11-15T10:05)
SRE Pager: paging eng-sre@ on-call if cert rollback needed. escalate in 10m if not mitigated. :alarm_clock:
Jules (oncall): impact assessment — approx 12% of requests routed to EU edge hit failing targets due to SNI mismatch, US/APAC fine. Customer-facing API generation calls are erroring with 502, some retries succeed.
CS Bot: Notifying CS: "Experiencing partial API errors in EU, investigating, will update in 15min"
Priya K: I can flip ALB target-group weights to drain the bad hosts as short term. Recommendations: 1) shift Route53 weighted routing away from eu-lb-1 -> eu-lb-2 (healthy) 2) mark unhealthy targets in ALB to force replacement 3) rollback cert-rotation if cert wrong.
Marco L: ALB describe-target-health snippet: ```{Target: i-0abc1234, State: unhealthy, Reason: TLS handshake failed} {Target: i-0def5678, State: healthy}```
Priya K: quick test: `openssl s_client -connect eu-lb-1:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com` -> shows cert CN=internal.lb.local.
Jules (oncall): OK plan: short-term weight shift + mark targets unhealthy; medium-term rollback cert rotation and re-run with correct SAN; long-term add SNI gating checks to rotation job.
Marco L: I'll run the weight shift. Performing `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://shift-weight.json` to move 70% traffic to eu-lb-2.
Priya K: also setting ALB target health to draining for the two bad instances: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:bad --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false` then `deregister-targets` to give time for graceful failover.
Jules (oncall): @SRE Pager please stand by to escalate to infra if Route53 change doesn't propagate in 5m. Route53 TTL is 300s, but there's risk of cached resolvers.
SRE Pager: acknowledged. PD escalation timer set for 10m.
Marco L: weight shift executed at 4332109789. Watching metrics...
Priya K: immediate drop in TLS errors from 9% -> 2.1% across EU edges, request success rate improving. latency back to baseline within 2 min.
CS Bot: Sent update to customers: "Partial EU API failures — traffic rerouted, attempting certificate rollback; ETA next update in 30m"
Jules (oncall): Good. Now attempting cert rollback. Marco, can you confirm which rotation job artifact to revert?
Marco L: yes — cert-rotation job `cert-rotation/2023-11-15T10:05` had wrong SAN. I'm initiating rollback to previous cert (id: cert-20231101). Running `deploybot rollback cert-rotation --to cert-20231101`.
Priya K: while rollback runs, tagging runbooks: `#runbook tls-handshake` — follow verify steps: `openssl s_client -connect` on each edge, `curl --resolve` to bypass DNS caching.
Jules (oncall): handed off primary to Marco in 10m box — I'm stepping out but will monitor. If any regression, @Marco L you're primary.
Marco L: done, rollback completed at 4332109899. Verified openssl shows CN=api.redwood-inference.com and SNI matches.
Priya K: re-registering drained targets one-by-one, running health checks. Monitoring for any surge in errors post-attach.
SRE Pager: PD note: incident acknowledged -> mitigated. Start timeline for postmortem.
Jules (oncall): impact summary for postmortem: root cause = cert rotation job published cert with internal CN causing SNI mismatch on subset of targets; contributing factor = insufficient post-rotation SNI validation and high Route53 TTL causing cached resolver traffic to hit bad targets longer.
CS Bot: Notified key customers and support; collecting logs for impacted customers for follow-up.
Marco L: action items: 1) add SNI verification step to rotation job (test cert SAN vs hostnames) 2) lower Route53 TTL temporarily for critical records during rotation 3) automate ALB target health check threshold alert.
Priya K: adding runbook updates and creating incident ticket INC-9943-postmortem and assigning to eng-sre team.
Jules (oncall): closing thread here; final note: thanks team, great quick coordination — please drop any logs/commands used into the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-9943 marked MITIGATED at 4332109923
